channel.title: The Frontier Gazeta
channel.description: A twice-weekly paper on what the frontier is saying: AI, venture, crypto, markets.

item.title: Friday, October 16, 2026
item.description: Across three shows this period, the underlying debate centered on the death of traditional software engineering and the lack of deterministic control over autonomous systems. This convergence spanned The Cognitive Revolution, How I Invest, and Odd Lots. Everett Hildenbrandt and Grigore Rosu of Runtime Verification argued that handwritten code will disappear within two years, replaced by formal specifications compiled into proofs by language models. On How I Invest, Betaworks founder John Borthwick agreed that software creation costs are collapsing to zero, shifting early-stage value from technical skill to founder taste and agent orchestration. Nate Soares of MIRI took the dark mechanical view on Odd Lots, warning that because frontier labs grow models through gradient descent rather than engineer them, developers cannot inspect the circuits dictating autonomous actions.
